newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, strong expectations for Dec.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, strong expectations for Dec.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Monday on an improving outlook for the market in December.
"Even though there were very few clients, the market rose strongly. There are good expectations for December," said a trader at an Argentine bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose 0.60 to 121.95, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 advanced 1/8 to 86-1/2.
The trader said the market feel good factor is being enforced by expectations that no negative news looms on the horizon.

"The decline in country risk is providing a better climate of confidence in Argentina, and this is reflected in the bond market," said analysts at financial consultancy C&E Consultores in an investor note. "Technically the signals are very good."

Even if the market is on the cusp of staging a late year rally, it is still suffering from poor volumes. That could change, however, if some of the overseas funds that have already booked profits this year come back to the market, traders say.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.85 percent from 5.48 percent.
